newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM says LWC price hike may signal upturn.
newsitem.headline: UPM says LWC price hike may signal upturn.

text.p: Finnish forest industry group UPM-Kymmene said late on Thursday that a planned hike in light-weight coated (LWC) paper prices it announced earlier this week might signal an upturn for the forest industry.

"It might (signal an upturn)... orderbooks are fatter now," CEO Juha Niemela said at a presentation to students when asked whether the hike, which UPM announced on Tuesday, signalled an upturn for the sector.
UPM said it would raise LWC paper prices by 5-8 percent during the first quarter of the year.
LWC's uses include magazines and direct mail order catalogues. Niemela said the price of magazine paper had dropped so low that there was a great need to raise it again.
LWC paper prices fell about 20 percent last year and it has been over 18 months since UPM announced any price increases for the grade.
UPM said on Tuesday pressure for price increases was especially strong in continental Europe and demand in January had been better than anticipated with customer stocks lower.
